N2_feedback_beyond_persistence.H1_primary: the full model has lower out-of-sample squared error with Diebold-Mariano p < 0.05 in at least 60% of included symbols
N2_feedback_beyond_persistence.fit_and_evaluate: OLS on 1-20 October; one-step squared errors on 21-30 October with the fitted coefficients
N2_feedback_beyond_persistence.reported_without_criterion: out-of-sample R^2 gain, MSE ratio and the cumulative response sum(beta) for every symbol
N2_feedback_beyond_persistence.restricted: dy_t = c + sum_{j=1..6} phi_j dy_{t-j} + e_t
N2_feedback_beyond_persistence.statistic: one-sided Diebold-Mariano test of equal squared error, Newey-West variance with 12 lags

N3_combined_response_from_flow.H1_primary: the interval for Psi excludes zero AND its half-width is below half of |Psi| in at least 80% of included symbols
N3_combined_response_from_flow.H2_secondary: Psi has the same sign on 1-15 October and 16-30 October in at least 80% of included symbols
N3_combined_response_from_flow.H3_secondary_root_T: the half-width on 1-10 October divided by the half-width on all 30 days lies in [1.2, 2.5] (root-T predicts sqrt(3) = 1.73) in at least 70% of included symbols
N3_combined_response_from_flow.estimand: combined response Psi = sum_{m=1..12} k_m, Newey-West 95% interval with 24 lags
N3_combined_response_from_flow.model: x_t = c + sum_{m=1..12} k_m r_{t-m} + u_t (one hour of lags), OLS on all 30 days

approved: Requested by the author in chat on 2026-10-31 ('new improved tests to run at Colab'); registered by this commit before any October 2026 data are opened.

data.dates: 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-30 inclusive (30 days); no other dates are read
data.grid: 5-minute grid over the 30 days, at the metrics snapshot times (minute multiple of 5, UTC)
data.inclusion: a symbol is included if at least 28 of the 30 days have both klines and metrics files and at least 90% of the 5-minute grid points have a finite class position and return; decided in the data stage before any estimate; no replacement symbols
data.source: data.binance.vision, futures/um/daily: 1-minute klines and 5-minute metrics; every file checked against Binance's .CHECKSUM (thesis/evidence/binance_vision.py, unchanged)

variables.class_position: y_t = log(sum_toptrader_long_short_ratio) at snapshot t (Binance's top-trader position ratio, a class-tagged position); dy_t = y_t - y_{t-5min}
variables.flow: x_t = sum over the five 1-minute bars ending at t of (2*taker_buy_quote_volume - quote_volume) divided by the sum of quote_volume (taker-flow imbalance, untagged)
variables.price: p_t = close of the 1-minute bar ending at snapshot time t

power_check: prereg/P1O_power_check.json (synthetic data only, 300 replications, Student-t(5) returns, 8,640 bars): N2's Diebold-Mariano test has power 0.66 at a population out-of-sample R^2 gain of 0.8% and 0.93 at 1.6%; N3's criterion has power 0.72 at a flow R^2 of 0.4% and 0.98 at 0.8%. Effects smaller than these will usually fail; that is part of the prediction.
question: On a data window that no earlier test has used (Binance USD-M futures, 1-30 October 2026), (N2) do price changes move a trader class's position beyond the persistence of that position, out of sample, as the closed-loop model's feedback channel requires; and (N3) does aggregate taker order flow identify the combined (merged) response to past returns at the root-T rate, as the theory predicts for flow data, in contrast with the earlier price-only test that failed (5 of 30)?
relation_to_paper: Results go into Paper 1's empirical section and Table tab:scorecard as new rows, pass or fail, labelled pre-specified; no earlier row changes.
runs: oct_tests.py is run once in Colab; its unlock counter (prereg/P1O_unlocks.json in the author's Drive) must read 1. A crash before results is reported, not hidden.
why_new: The earlier state-tracking result passed but was explained by the persistence of the target, and the earlier price-only combined-response test failed. N2 measures the feedback channel net of persistence, out of sample. N3 uses flow data, which the theory says identify the combined response, and checks the root-T rate. Neither re-scores or redefines an earlier test; the earlier results stand as reported.
